records.source: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ ἀρνίον ἑστὸς ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σιών, καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ἔχουσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένον ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And I saw, and behold the Lamb standing on the Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 having the name of him and the name of the Father of him having been written on the foreheads of them.
pieces: I looked, and I saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion. With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} stood 144,000 people, whose foreheads bore {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father.

L.1: And I looked, and look, the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 144,000 who had {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and the name of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father written on their foreheads.

R.1: Then I looked, and I saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion. With {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were 144,000 people. His name and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Father's name were written on their foreheads.

decisions.choice: Mount Zion: the place where God's king reigns and his people are gathered
decisions.reason: Zion is Jerusalem's hill, where God set his king (Psalm 2:6) and where those who call on the LORD will be saved (Joel 2:32). Hebrews 12:22 speaks of the heavenly Mount Zion. The song in 14:2-3 is heard from heaven, but whether John sees the Lamb in heaven or on earth is not said.

decisions.choice: the 144,000 with the name: God's sealed people
decisions.reason: They are the 144,000 sealed in 7:3-8; see the note on 7:4. The seal is now shown to be the name of the Lamb and his Father, in contrast to the beast's mark and name (13:16-17).

records.heading: The Lamb and the 144,000

records.source: καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὡς φωνὴν ὑδάτων πολλῶν καὶ ὡς φωνὴν βροντῆς μεγάλης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς κιθαρῳδῶν κιθαριζόντων ἐν ταῖς κιθάραις αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And I heard a voice out of the heaven as voice of waters many and as voice of thunder great, and the voice which I heard as of harpists harping on the harps of them.
pieces: From heaven I heard a sound like the voice of many waters and of great thunder, and the sound was that of harpists playing on their harps.

L.2: And I heard a sound from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of great thunder, and the sound that I heard [was] like harpists playing on their harps.

R.2: I heard a sound from heaven. It was as loud as a great waterfall and as loud as thunder. But it also sounded like people playing harps.

decisions.choice: one sound, mighty and musical
decisions.reason: φωνὴν means voice or sound. The sound is as overwhelming as a great flood or thunder (compare 1:15; 19:6), and yet it is music.

records.source: καὶ ᾄδουσιν ὡς ᾠδὴν καινὴν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων· καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο μαθεῖν τὴν ᾠδὴν εἰ μὴ αἱ ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες, οἱ ἠγορασμένοι ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And they sing as a song new before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one was able to learn the song except the 144,000, those having been bought from the earth.
pieces: Before the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders they sing what seems a new song, a song no one could learn except the 144,000 bought out of the earth.

L.3: And they sing [as it were] a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders, and no one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been bought from the earth.

R.3: They were singing a new song in front of the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders. Only the 144,000 people who had been bought back from the earth could learn the song.

decisions.choice: only the redeemed can learn the song
decisions.reason: The new song (5:9) celebrates redemption, and only those who have been bought by the Lamb can learn it. ἠγορασμένοι is the word of 5:9: bought at the price of his blood.

records.source: οὗτοί εἰσιν οἳ μετὰ γυναικῶν οὐκ ἐμολύνθησαν, παρθένοι γάρ εἰσιν· οὗτοι οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες τῷ ἀρνίῳ ὅπου ἂν ὑπάγῃ· οὗτοι ἠγοράσθησαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπαρχὴ τῷ θεῷ καὶ τῷ ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτῶν οὐχ εὑρέθη ψεῦδος· ἄμωμοί εἰσιν.
records.gloss: These are who with women not were defiled, for virgins they are. These the [ones] following the Lamb wherever he goes. These were bought from the men as firstfruits to the God and to the Lamb, \v 5 and in the mouth of them not was found a lie; blameless they are.
pieces: These have kept themselves from being defiled with women; they are virgins. They are the followers of the Lamb, going wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} goes. From among {{gender:humankind|mankind}} they were bought as firstfruits for God and for the Lamb,
and no lie was found in what they said; they are without blemish.

L.4: These are the ones who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} goes. These were bought from among {{gender:people|men}} as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,
L.5: and in their mouth no lie was found; they are blameless.

R.4: These people did not make themselves unclean with women. They kept themselves pure, like virgins. They follow the Lamb wherever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} goes. They were bought back from among all people to be the first part of the harvest, given to God and the Lamb.
R.5: They never told lies. They have done nothing wrong.

decisions.choice: virgins: kept pure from idolatry, wholly devoted to the Lamb
alternatives: soldiers keeping the purity required in holy war
decisions.reason: The prophets call Israel's idolatry adultery and prostitution, and Revelation calls Babylon a prostitute who corrupts the nations (2:20-22; 17:1-5). The 144,000 have not committed that unfaithfulness: they belong to the Lamb alone, like a bride (19:7-8; 2 Corinthians 11:2). The picture may also draw on the rule that Israel's soldiers kept themselves from women before battle (Deuteronomy 23:9-10; 1 Samuel 21:5), since the 144,000 are counted like an army (7:4-8). Nothing in the New Testament makes marriage defiling (Hebrews 13:4), so a literal reading about celibacy is unlikely.

decisions.choice: firstfruits: the first part of the harvest, given to God
decisions.reason: The first and best of the harvest was offered to God as a pledge that the whole belonged to him (Exodus 23:19). The redeemed are firstfruits, a sign of the harvest still to come (14:15-16; compare James 1:18).

decisions.choice: no lie in their mouth: Zephaniah 3:13
decisions.reason: Zephaniah foretold a remnant who "shall speak no lies, nor shall there be found in their mouth a deceitful tongue" (Zephaniah 3:13; compare Isaiah 53:9 of the servant). In a book where the beast and the false prophet deceive (13:14), they hold to the truth. ἄμωμοί is the word for an unblemished sacrifice.

decisions.choice: virgins (L, B); pure, like virgins (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Greek word; Readable shows that it is a picture of purity (m1).

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον πετόμενον ἐν μεσουρανήματι, ἔχοντα εὐαγγέλιον αἰώνιον εὐαγγελίσαι ἐπὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶν ἔθνος καὶ φυλὴν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ λαόν, λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Φοβήθητε τὸν θεὸν καὶ δότε αὐτῷ δόξαν, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα τῆς κρίσεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ προσκυνήσατε τῷ ποιήσαντι τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ θάλασσαν καὶ πηγὰς ὑδάτων.
records.gloss: And I saw another angel flying in mid-heaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those sitting on the earth and to every nation and tribe and tongue and people, \v 7 saying with a voice loud: Fear the God and give him glory, because came the hour of the judgment of him, and worship the [one] having made the heaven and the earth and sea and springs of waters.
pieces: I saw another angel too, flying high in the sky, who carried an eternal gospel to proclaim to the people who live on the earth, to every nation, tribe, language, and people.

In a loud voice he cried, "Stand in awe of God and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory, for the hour has come when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will judge. Worship the maker of heaven and earth, of the sea and the springs of water."

L.6: And I saw another angel flying in mid-heaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who live on the earth, and to every nation and tribe and language and people,
L.7: saying with a loud voice, "Fear God and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory, because the hour of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgment has come, and worship the one who made heaven and the earth and sea and springs of waters."

R.6: Then I saw another angel flying high in the sky. He had the eternal good news to tell the people who live on the earth, people of every nation, tribe, language, and people.
R.7: He shouted, "Honor God with fear and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory! The time has come for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to judge. Worship God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and the springs of water!"

decisions.choice: an eternal gospel: God's lasting good news, offered to all
decisions.reason: Before the final judgments, the good news is proclaimed to every people. Its call is to fear God, give him glory and worship him as Creator, the response the plagues did not bring (9:20-21) and some gave after the witnesses rose (11:13). It is called eternal because God's purpose and offer do not change.

decisions.choice: the maker of heaven, earth, sea and springs: the Creator
decisions.reason: The words echo Exodus 20:11 and Psalm 146:6. The four realms match the four trumpets that struck the earth, sea, springs and sky (8:7-12).

decisions.choice: those who sit on the earth: its inhabitants
decisions.reason: καθημένους, "sitting", is used here for living on the earth, like the more usual "those who dwell on the earth" (3:10).

decisions.choice: gospel (L, B); good news (R)
decisions.reason: As the key-term list has it.

decisions.choice: Fear (L); Stand in awe of (B); Honor ... with fear (R)
decisions.reason: To fear God is to honor him with reverence; Balanced and Readable bring out that sense.

records.heading: Three angels

records.source: Καὶ ἄλλος δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἠκολούθησεν λέγων· Ἔπεσεν, ἔπεσεν Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἣ ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς πεπότικεν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη.
records.gloss: And another angel, a second, followed saying: Fell, fell Babylon the great, which of the wine of the passion of the immorality of her has given to drink all the nations.
pieces: Another angel, a second one, came after him and said, "Babylon the great has fallen, has fallen! She made all the nations drink the wine of her raging immorality."

L.8: And another angel, a second, followed, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all the nations drink of the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality."

R.8: A second angel followed the first. He said, "Babylon the great has fallen! It has fallen! Babylon made all the nations drink the wine of her sexual sins and go wild with it."

decisions.choice: Fallen, fallen is Babylon: Isaiah and Jeremiah
decisions.reason: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon" is the cry of Isaiah 21:9. Jeremiah 51:7-8 says that Babylon was a golden cup that made all the earth drunk, and that she has suddenly fallen. The fall is announced here before it is described in chapters 17-18.

decisions.choice: Babylon the great: the city of the world opposed to God
decisions.reason: Babylon destroyed Jerusalem and exiled God's people, and became a byword for proud power set against God. 1 Peter 5:13 appears to use "Babylon" for Rome, and the details of Revelation 17-18 fit Rome in John's day. But the city stands for every such power, which seduces the nations and persecutes God's people.

decisions.choice: the wine of the passion of her immorality
alternatives: the wine of the wrath that comes on her immorality
decisions.reason: θυμοῦ means passion or fury. Babylon makes the nations drunk with a passion for her immorality, her idolatry and its pleasures; and the same word in 14:10 is God's fury that answers it. The double sense is likely intended.

records.source: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος τρίτος ἠκολούθησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Εἴ τις προσκυνεῖ τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ λαμβάνει χάραγμα ἐπὶ τοῦ μετώπου αὐτοῦ ἢ ἐπὶ τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς πίεται ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ κεκερασμένου ἀκράτου ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ, καὶ βασανισθήσεται ἐν πυρὶ καὶ θείῳ ἐνώπιον ἀγγέλων ἁγίων καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ ἀρνίου.
records.gloss: And another angel, a third, followed them saying with voice loud: If anyone worships the beast and the image of it and receives a mark on the forehead of him or on the hand of him, \v 10 also he will drink of the wine of the fury of the God the having been mixed undiluted in the cup of the wrath of him, and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur before angels holy and before the Lamb.
pieces: A third angel followed them, calling out in a loud voice: "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and takes its mark on the forehead or the hand,

{{gender:they|he}} will also drink the wine of God's fury, unwatered, mixed in the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, and will suffer torment in fire and sulfur before the holy angels and before the Lamb.

L.9: And another angel, a third, followed them, saying with a loud voice, "If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives a mark on {{gender:their|his}} forehead or on {{gender:their|his}} hand,
L.10: {{gender:that person|he}} also will drink of the wine of God's fury, mixed undiluted in the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath, and will be tormented with fire and sulfur before holy angels and before the Lamb.

R.9: Then a third angel followed them. He shouted, "Anyone who worships the beast and its statue and gets its mark on the forehead or hand
R.10: will drink the wine of God's anger. It will be poured into the cup of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger at full strength. They will suffer in burning sulfur in front of the holy angels and the Lamb.

decisions.choice: the cup of God's wrath
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God's judgment as a cup that the nations must drink (Jeremiah 25:15-16; Psalm 75:9; Isaiah 51:17). Wine was usually mixed with water; this is undiluted, full strength. Those who drank Babylon's wine (14:8) drink God's.

decisions.choice: fire and sulfur: the judgment of Sodom
decisions.reason: See the note on 9:17. Fire and sulfur fell on Sodom (Genesis 19:24) and belong to the final judgment in Revelation (19:20; 20:10; 21:8).

decisions.choice: torment before the Lamb: the final judgment of those who worship the beast
decisions.reason: The warning is severe and is meant to keep believers from worshiping the beast whatever it costs (14:12). It is given in the language of prophetic images: fire, sulfur, and smoke rising forever (Isaiah 34:9-10). Christians have understood the nature and duration of final punishment in different ways; this note does not decide between them. The judgment takes place in the presence of the Lamb, who was slaughtered for the world: it is just, and it is his.

decisions.choice: undiluted (L); unwatered (B); at full strength (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says that the wine is not mixed with water (m1).

records.source: καὶ ὁ καπνὸς τοῦ βασανισμοῦ αὐτῶν εἰς αἰῶνας αἰώνων ἀναβαίνει, καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνάπαυσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, οἱ προσκυνοῦντες τὸ θηρίον καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἴ τις λαμβάνει τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And the smoke of the torment of them into ages of ages goes up, and not they have rest day and night, those worshiping the beast and the image of it, and if anyone receives the mark of the name of it.
pieces: Forever and ever the smoke of their torment goes up; day and night they have no rest, the worshipers of the beast and its image, and all who take the mark of its name."

L.11: And the smoke of their torment goes up for ages of ages, and they have no rest day and night, those who worship the beast and its image, and whoever receives the mark of its name."

R.11: The smoke from their suffering will rise forever and ever. Those who worship the beast and its statue, and anyone who gets the mark of its name, will have no rest, day or night."

decisions.choice: smoke rising forever: Isaiah 34:10
decisions.reason: Isaiah said of Edom's judgment that "its smoke shall go up forever" (Isaiah 34:10). See the note on 14:10.

decisions.choice: no rest day and night
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used of the living creatures, who never rest from praising God (4:8). The worshipers of the beast have no rest from torment, while those who die in the Lord rest from their labors (14:13).

records.source: Ὧδε ἡ ὑπομονὴ τῶν ἁγίων ἐστίν, οἱ τηροῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν πίστιν Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: Here the endurance of the saints is, those keeping the commandments of the God and the faith of Jesus.
pieces: This is where God's holy people need endurance, those who keep God's commandments and hold to their faith in Jesus.

L.12: Here is the endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.

R.12: This is why God's people must keep going. They obey God's commands and keep their faith in Jesus.

decisions.choice: the faith of Jesus: faith in Jesus
decisions.reason: πίστιν Ἰησοῦ can mean faith in Jesus, faithfulness to him, or Jesus's own faithfulness. Beside "keep the commandments of God", it most likely means holding on to faith in him (compare 2:13, "my faith").

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λεγούσης· Γράψον· Μακάριοι οἱ νεκροὶ οἱ ἐν κυρίῳ ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἀπ’ ἄρτι.
records.gloss: And I heard a voice out of the heaven saying: Write: Blessed the dead the [ones] in Lord dying from now.
pieces: A voice from heaven spoke to me: "Write: From now on, how blessed are the dead who die in the Lord!"

L.13: And I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Write: Blessed are the dead who die in [the] Lord from now on."

R.13: Then I heard a voice from heaven. It said, "Write this: From now on, God blesses the people who belong to the Lord when they die."

decisions.choice: the second blessing: those who die in the Lord
decisions.reason: This is the second of the book's seven blessings (1:3). To die "in the Lord" is to die belonging to Christ and joined to him, whether by martyrdom or not.

decisions.choice: "from now on" ends the blessing
alternatives: "from now on" begins the Spirit's reply: "From now on, yes, says the Spirit"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts "from now on" with the blessing: those who die from this time forward are blessed. Some take it with what follows. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: God blesses (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:3, Readable names God as the one who blesses.

records.source: ναί, λέγει τὸ πνεῦμα, ἵνα ἀναπαήσονται ἐκ τῶν κόπων αὐτῶν, τὰ γὰρ ἔργα αὐτῶν ἀκολουθεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Yes, says the Spirit, so that they will rest from the labors of them, for the works of them follow with them.
pieces: "Indeed," the Spirit says, "let them rest from their toil, for what they have done goes with them."

L.13: "Yes," says the Spirit, "so that they will rest from their labors, for their works follow with them."

R.13: "Yes," says the Spirit. "They will rest from their hard work, because the good things they have done go with them."

decisions.choice: so that they will rest: a result or a wish
decisions.reason: ἵνα with a future verb here gives the result of the blessing, or expresses a wish: let them rest.

decisions.choice: their works follow them: what they did is remembered and rewarded
decisions.reason: Their labors end, but their works go with them before God. Christ gives to each according to their works (2:23; 22:12).

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ νεφέλη λευκή, καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν νεφέλην καθήμενον ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἔχων ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ στέφανον χρυσοῦν καὶ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ δρέπανον ὀξύ.
records.gloss: And I saw, and behold a cloud white, and on the cloud sitting [one] like a son of man, having on the head of him a crown golden and in the hand of him a sickle sharp.
pieces: Then I saw a white cloud, and on it sat one like a son of man. A gold crown was on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head, and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand a sharp sickle.

L.14: And I looked, and look, a white cloud, and seated on the cloud [one] like a son of man, having a golden crown on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head and a sharp sickle in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

R.14: Then I looked, and I saw a white cloud. Someone like a son of man was sitting on it. He wore a gold crown on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head and held a sharp sickle in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand.

decisions.choice: one like a son of man: Christ, coming to harvest the earth
alternatives: an angel, since the next figure is "another angel" (14:15)
decisions.reason: The phrase is Daniel's (7:13), used of Christ in 1:13, and the figure sits on a cloud, as Christ comes with the clouds (1:7). He wears a victor's crown. Some take him for an angel because 14:15 speaks of "another angel" and because an angel gives him his order. Most take him to be Christ, who reaps the harvest at the end (Matthew 13:39-41).

decisions.choice: a sickle: the harvest of the end
decisions.reason: "Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe" (Joel 3:13). Jesus spoke of the harvest at the end of the age (Matthew 13:30, 39; Mark 4:29).

records.heading: The harvest of the earth

records.source: καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ κράζων ἐν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης· Πέμψον τὸ δρέπανόν σου καὶ θέρισον, ὅτι ἦλθεν ἡ ὥρα θερίσαι, ὅτι ἐξηράνθη ὁ θερισμὸς τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And another angel came out out of the temple crying in voice loud to the [one] sitting on the cloud: Send the sickle of you and reap, because came the hour to reap, because was dried the harvest of the earth.
pieces: Out of the temple came another angel, crying aloud to the one seated on the cloud, "Swing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sickle and gather the harvest! The hour for reaping is here; the earth's harvest is dry and ready."

L.15: And another angel came out of the temple, crying out with a loud voice to the one seated on the cloud, "Send {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come, for the harvest of the earth has become dry."

R.15: Another angel came out of the temple. He shouted to the one sitting on the cloud, "Use {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sickle and harvest the crops! It is time to harvest. The crops on the earth are ripe."

decisions.choice: the grain harvest: the gathering of God's people, or judgment
alternatives: judgment on the world, like the grape harvest that follows
decisions.reason: Jesus used the grain harvest for the gathering of his people (Matthew 13:30; John 4:35-38), and here the reaper is the one like a son of man with no mention of wrath. The grape harvest that follows (14:17-20) is plainly judgment. Many therefore read the first harvest as the gathering of the redeemed and the second as judgment; others take both as judgment, as in Joel 3:13.

decisions.choice: the order comes from the temple
decisions.reason: The angel comes from the temple, God's presence: the time of the harvest is set by God (compare Mark 13:32).

decisions.choice: dried: fully ripe
decisions.reason: ἐξηράνθη means dried up, the state of grain ready for cutting.

decisions.choice: your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The angel speaks to the one like a son of man, Christ (14:14), so "your" takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῆς νεφέλης τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐθερίσθη ἡ γῆ.
records.gloss: And cast the [one] sitting on the cloud the sickle of him on the earth, and was reaped the earth.
pieces: The one on the cloud swept {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sickle across the earth, and the earth's harvest was gathered in.

L.16: And the one seated on the cloud cast {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sickle on the earth, and the earth was reaped.

R.16: So the one sitting on the cloud swung {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sickle over the earth, and the crops were harvested.

decisions.choice: the harvest is brief and complete
decisions.reason: The account is short: one swing of the sickle, and the earth is reaped.

records.source: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ἔχων καὶ αὐτὸς δρέπανον ὀξύ.
records.gloss: And another angel came out out of the temple the in the heaven, having also he a sickle sharp.
pieces: Then from the temple in heaven came yet another angel, also holding a sharp sickle.

L.17: And another angel came out of the temple in heaven, he too having a sharp sickle.

R.17: Then another angel came out of the temple in heaven. He also had a sharp sickle.

decisions.choice: a second harvest
decisions.reason: A second reaper comes, this time an angel, for the grape harvest.

records.source: καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἐκ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὁ ἔχων ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρός, καὶ ἐφώνησεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τῷ ἔχοντι τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ λέγων· Πέμψον σου τὸ δρέπανον τὸ ὀξὺ καὶ τρύγησον τοὺς βότρυας τῆς ἀμπέλου τῆς γῆς, ὅτι ἤκμασαν αἱ σταφυλαὶ αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And another angel out of the altar, the [one] having authority over the fire, and he called with voice loud to the [one] having the sickle the sharp, saying: Send of you the sickle the sharp and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because ripened the grapes of it.
pieces: And another angel came from the altar, the angel with power over the fire. In a great voice he called to the one holding the sharp sickle, "Swing your sharp sickle and cut the bunches from the vine of the earth, for its grapes are at their ripest."

L.18: And another angel [came] out from the altar, the one who has authority over the fire, and he called with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, saying, "Send your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for its grapes are ripe."

R.18: Then another angel came from the altar. He was in charge of the fire. He shouted to the angel with the sharp sickle, "Use your sharp sickle and cut the bunches of grapes from the vine of the earth. The grapes are ripe."

decisions.choice: from the altar, with power over fire: the prayers answered
decisions.reason: The altar is where the souls cried for justice (6:9-10) and where the prayers rose and fire was thrown on the earth (8:3-5). The grape harvest answers those prayers.

decisions.choice: the vintage of the earth: judgment
decisions.reason: Joel 3:13 joins the sickle with the winepress full of the nations' wickedness, and Isaiah 63:1-6 pictures God treading the nations in the winepress of his wrath.

records.source: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸ δρέπανον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ἐτρύγησεν τὴν ἄμπελον τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν ληνὸν τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν μέγαν.
records.gloss: And cast the angel the sickle of him into the earth and gathered the vine of the earth and cast into the winepress of the fury of the God the great.
pieces: The angel swept his sickle across the earth, cut the earth's vintage, and flung it into the winepress of God's fury, the great winepress.

L.19: And the angel cast his sickle to the earth and gathered the vintage of the earth and threw [it] into the great winepress of the fury of God.

R.19: So the angel swung his sickle over the earth. He cut the grapes and threw them into the huge winepress of God's anger.

decisions.choice: the winepress: a pit where grapes were trodden underfoot
decisions.reason: Grapes were crushed by treading them in a stone or rock-cut press, and the juice ran out into a lower vat. The picture of God's wrath as a winepress comes from Isaiah 63:3 and Lamentations 1:15. The Greek pairs a feminine noun with a masculine adjective, "great", which may stress the adjective.

records.source: καὶ ἐπατήθη ἡ ληνὸς ἔξωθεν τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αἷμα ἐκ τῆς ληνοῦ ἄχρι τῶν χαλινῶν τῶν ἵππων ἀπὸ σταδίων χιλίων ἑξακοσίων.
records.gloss: And was trodden the winepress outside the city, and came out blood out of the winepress up to the bridles of the horses, from stadia 1,600.
pieces: Outside the city the winepress was trodden, and out of it came blood, up to the horses' bridles, for {{units:about 180 miles|1,600 stadia}}.

L.20: And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress up to the bridles of the horses, for 1,600 stadia.

R.20: The grapes were crushed in the winepress outside the city. Blood flowed out of the winepress. It came up as high as the horses' heads and spread for {{units:about 180 miles|1,600 stadia}}.

decisions.choice: outside the city: judgment beyond the city of God
decisions.reason: The city is most likely the holy city, God's people (11:2; 20:9). Judgment falls outside it. Jesus also suffered outside the city gate (Hebrews 13:12).

decisions.choice: blood to the horses' bridles for 1,600 stadia: a judgment of immense scale
decisions.reason: A stadion was about 600 feet, so 1,600 stadia is about 180 miles. The number may be symbolic (forty times forty, or four squared times a hundred, the four corners of the earth), and it is roughly the length of the land of Israel. The picture of blood up to the horses' bridles anticipates the battle of 19:11-21.

decisions.choice: units: about 180 miles | 1,600 stadia
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek measure; Balanced and Readable give a modern equivalent, with the original as the alternative.
